overview: White plays 2.g4 to gain space on the kingside and prepare Bg2 or g5, aiming at a quick kingside initiative against the Caro-Kann. After 2...d5 White either plays 3.e5 for a space gambit or 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.d3, the Scorpion-Grob Gambit, handing over the e-pawn. Black normally meets it by capturing and keeping solid.

white_ideas.idea: Gain space with g4-g5 and Bg2
Use the h-file or the g-pawn for an early attack

black_ideas.idea: Take on e4 and return material only if it helps development
Play ...Bxg4 or ...h5 to punish the weakening

typical_structures.structure: Open e-file after dxe4 and exd3
White pawns advanced on g4 against ...c6/...d5 set-up

character.notes: The extra pawn pushes lead to a risky position where White loosened the king.

gambit.notes: In the main subtree 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.d3 offers the e-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Spike is regarded as a risky surprise weapon that Black meets without difficulty.

structure.notes: Ends up with exchanged central pawns and an open e-file in the gambit lines.

approach.notes: Strong players rarely meet the Caro-Kann with 2.g4.

level.notes: Dubious, so a poor choice for a first repertoire.

sublines_that_differ.name: Quiet 3.e5
sublines_that_differ.how: White tries a space-gaining line without giving a pawn, and Black attacks g4 with ...h5 or ...Bg4.

character.reason: An early g4 loosens White's king and the play becomes concrete and double-edged.

gambit.reason: The most played subtree line 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.d3 gives a pawn that Black may keep.

soundness.reason: Strong players regard the Spike as a loosening surprise that Black can meet comfortably.

structure.reason: The e-file opens after the exchanges but the Caro-Kann c6 pawn structure stays.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom play 2.g4 against the Caro-Kann.

level.reason: A dubious line is not Beginner and it asks for no deep theory.

plans.reason: White hopes to use fast development and a g-pawn advance for an attack.
